https://www.christiandaily.com/news/war-.text: Volunteer offering help at the Romania-Ukraine border Photo by Michel E / Unsplash European Christian Mission International (ECMI) reports that 160 churches have been planted across Europe by displaced Ukrainians in the four years since Russia invaded their country. In a report, ECMI said that what began as a devastating displacement through war is becoming an unexpected movement of gospel witness across Europe. “Ukrainian believers, carrying deep pain and loss, are also carrying the hope of Christ wherever they go,” said the ECMI report. Jim Memory, Strategic Partnerships Director for ECMI and Co-Regional Director for Lausanne Europe, attended a recent Ukrainian Baptist Churches in Europe Conference in Poland and came away deeply encouraged by what God is doing through Ukrainian Christians across the continent. Memory disclosed how inspiring it was to hear story after story of faithfulness under pressure. “It was a privilege to listen to their stories, make connections, and briefly speak,” he said. Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, millions of Ukrainians have been forced to flee their homes, said the report. “Yet in the midst of grief, separation, and uncertainty, God’s light is shining brighter. Among Baptists alone, around 160 Ukrainian churches have been planted across Europe during the past four years.” The report added, “Increasingly, Ukrainian believers are refusing to see themselves only as refugees. “Instead, many are embracing a different calling - missionaries sent by God into the nations of Europe.” ECMI reflected on how the Kingdom of God advanced through tragedy in the book of Acts and compared that reality with the church planting being carried out by Ukrainians displaced by war. When persecution scattered the first Christians, the gospel spread wherever they went, said the report. What looked like tragedy became the very means by which the Kingdom of God advanced. “Ukrainian Christians are arriving in unfamiliar countries carrying trauma and heartbreak, yet many are also bringing courage, prayer, hospitality, evangelistic passion, and a deep dependence on God,” said the report. “New fellowships are forming. Churches are being planted. People are hearing about Jesus through those who themselves have suffered greatly. “Their witness is a powerful reminder that darkness does not have the final word. http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/31/euras.text: The annual Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit is gathering a diverse group of world leaders from 21 countries in Kyrgyzstan’s capital Bishkek, as they pursue new alliances, ambitions and opportunities with the rise of regional powers in the rapidly evolving multipolar Eurasia.The two-day summit kicked off on Monday, focusing on political, economic and security engagements and cooperation, a long-promised development bank, connectivity, energy and trade routes strained by wars and conflicts, and the defining challenges of the Global South. The SCO’s 10 members — China, India, Pakistan, Russia, Belarus, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan — speak for more than 40% of the world's population.The bloc increasingly bills itself as an alternative to a Western-led order, as it is joined by leaders of at least 15 states as “dialogue partners,” spanning Central Asia and the rest of the continent, the South Caucasus, as well as the Middle East, including Turkey, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Vietnam, as well as Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan and Armenia.The bloc, which marked its 25th anniversary, was formed to address regional security issues after the collapse of the Soviet Union, but over time it has evolved into a powerhouse of multi-layered trade, security and political cooperation.The theme of the summit, “25 years of the SCO: together for sustainable peace, development and prosperity”, is a message in itself to the world as the 21 leaders convene to formulate answers, build influence — and possibly new alliances to the rapidly changing world. China’s Xi Jinping, India’s Narendra Modi, Turkey’s Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, together with other presidents and prime ministers, including Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian as well as UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, arrived in Bishkek on Monday to hold a series of bilateral meetings and later attending the opening of the World Nomad Games, a traditional Central Asian sports and culture event.The SCO announced that Russia’s war in Ukraine, the Iran war with its far-reaching global economic consequences, as well as the push of the major and middle powers in the SCO for wider global influence, are among the main topics of this year’s gathering, while the host country Kyrgyzstan is aiming to advance the establishment of a SCO Development Fund and an Investment Fund for major projects.Developing economic connectivity opportunities, including new energy and transport corridors, is also a key objective as the Iran war reshapes the world’s transit and supply chains.'Golden period' of tiesHost of the summit Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov welcomed his Chinese counterpart Xi on his arrival in Bishkek, and the two leaders signed a treaty on “eternal good-neighbourliness, friendship and cooperation,” which, the Kyrgyz presidency said in a statement, acts as a comprehensive strategic partnership in the new era. Xi described the China-Kyrgyzstan ties as a “golden period” of development. Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov also held a flurry of bilateral talks on Monday with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh, Lao President Thongloun Sisoulith, Togolese President Faure Gnassingbe and Vietnamese Vice President Vo Thi Anh Xuan as well as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.As the US and the EU are actively increasing their presence in Central Asia, China is also pushing for a rapid economic engagement across Central Asia, with major transport and infrastructure projects being developed to connect China and the West through Central Asia, such as the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, which is expected to shorten transport routes between Asia, the Middle East and southern Europe.As industrial cooperation and transport connectivity are major priorities for Tashkent, Uzbekistan’s President Shavkat Mirziyoyev arrived in Bishkek to also promote the Trans-Afghan Corridor connecting the rapidly developing infrastructure projects of Central Asia’s countries to Afghanistan and ports on the Indian Ocean.Azerbaijan’s President Ilham Aliyev and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan held a new round of peace talks in Bishkek on Monday to discuss the former rivals’ next steps in their historic peace process.The two leaders also discussed new trade and energy cooperation as well as the key Middle Corridor projects through the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP).Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev also met his Azerbaijani counterpart to discuss trade and investments through joint regional projects.Putin also arrived in Bishkek on Monday to make his mark on the regional summit and will meet Xi amid Moscow's faltering economy.The Russian president is scheduled to meet Erdoğan to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine and Black Sea security, as well as Iran's Pezeshkian, as Moscow has been a strong supporter of Iran during its military confrontation with the United States and Israel.Putin is also expected to meet Pashinyan following Moscow’s warnings against Yerevan’s newly announced intention to apply for EU membership.

http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27926.text: Big News Network.com Latvia's military threat level unchanged: PM RIGA, Aug. 27 (Xinhua) -- Latvia's military threat level has not changed and the risk of a "direct Russian military invasion" remains low, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said on Thursday, seeking to reassure the public after a proposed emergency measure for the country's eastern border region raised concern. Kulbergs made the remarks after the country's Climate and Energy Ministry submitted a draft government order on Wednesday proposing a temporary state of emergency in the healthcare, energy supply and water management sectors in Latvia's eastern border region until Dec. 1 to ensure critical services could continue operating during an airspace threat. "I want to make it clear to the people of Latvia that there is currently no reason for concern. Latvia's military threat level has not changed," Kulbergs said, citing assessments by the country's security authorities. The proposal drew public attention because it referred to the "threat of an escalation in Russian military actions" in explaining the need for the measure. Kulbergs said such wording, when separated from the actual security assessment, had caused questions and concern. The ministry withdrew the draft on Thursday for revision and said it would change the document's title following public discussion and what it described as inaccurate interpretations of its purpose. Kulbergs said Latvia must remain prepared for hybrid threats, including cyberattacks, attempted sabotage, provocations and incidents involving unmanned aerial vehicles. The prime minister also urged ministries, politicians and government officials to communicate security measures clearly, saying technical and organizational preparedness measures should not be presented as if Latvia were "on the brink of war." https://hungarytoday.hu/wizz-air-reporte.text: Wizz Air Reportedly Plans Major Layoffs in Neighboring Country Budapest-based Wizz Air could be planning significant layoffs in Romania. According to an internal document obtained by an online news outlet, a total of 172 employees could be affected. According to a document obtained by Romanian news outlet APIX.ro , 172 of Wizz Air’s 1,892 employees in Romania could be affected, representing nearly ten percent of the company’s local workforce. The planned layoffs would affect non-management positions at all four bases involved, primarily among flight crews. Over 150 pilots and co-pilots and more than 120 cabin crew members are on the list. The largest number of positions could be eliminated in Craiova, where 47 employees could be placed on the layoff list. In Bucharest, 46 employees could be affected, compared with 44 in Iași and 36 in Cluj. The list includes five captain positions, six first officer positions, six senior cabin attendant positions and 19 cabin crew positions. The company has established two criteria for selecting employees who could be affected. Performance evaluations would be considered first, particularly the results of the most recent annual review. If that does not establish a clear ranking among employees, length of service within the Wizz Air Group could be used as the deciding factor. The layoffs are currently scheduled to take place in October and November, with employment contracts ending when the applicable notice periods expire. The Wizz Air trade union has until September 14 to submit its position on the planned layoffs. The final number of employees affected will depend on consultations with employees and the union. Wizz Air is also preparing for higher fares and capacity cuts, developments that could affect Hungarian travelers as well, Világgazdaság reports. According to the Hungarian low-cost carrier, persistently high oil and jet fuel prices are likely to put continued cost pressure on the European aviation industry. It remains unclear, however, exactly how these factors will affect airfares in 2027. The developments lend some support, though do not prove recent comments made by Ryanair CEO Michael O’Leary that consolidation could soon take place in the European aviation market. Amid the uncertainty surrounding easyJet, he said the process may already have begun. Although Wizz Air has not made any significant response to the comments, O’Leary has said that Wizz Air itself has become a potential takeover target and that a deal could be completed as early as this year. Against this backdrop, Wizz Air has also announced plans to take over the entire domestic route network of state-owned Romanian airline Tarom. Wizz Air CEO József Váradi says Romania does not need a loss-making national airline. https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/black-c.text: This is the moment a twisted 'copycat killer' was arrested in hospital after lying about how he had accidentally sliced his own hand as he tried to sever a woman's body. Forensics student Benjamin Day dialled 999 for help after using gaffer tape to bind a deep cut to his left hand, sustained as he tried to dismember sex worker Maria Saceanu's body. The 20-year-old only 'wanted help with his own injury' so stopped his 'gruesome task' and left his victim's naked body on the floor of the 'kill room' at an Airbnb in Oldbury. But he tried to convince police he had been bitten by a fox or wild dog. After his 'meticulous' plan 'all went wrong', he walked 20 minutes away from the Airbnb in Barncroft Road, in Tividale, in a failed bid to get his wound treated so he could head back to continue with his horrific crime. He was 'still hoping to get away with what he had done and still thinking about covering his tracks', Wolverhampton Crown Court was told. His murder chamber had been styled based on the US TV series Dexter - a show he was said to have been obsessed with. Day, of Yeadon Close, Redditch, Worcestershire , had denied murdering Ms Saceanu between December 19 and 22, 2025. But the University of Worcester student changed his plea in a dramatic court U-turn on the second day of his trial at Wolverhampton Crown Court on Tuesday, October 6. He now faces life behind bars and will be sentenced on Friday, December 4. READ MORE: Lodger at Oldbury Airbnb 'alarmed after blood trail left behind by Dexter copycat killer' - trial hears Body-worn footage released by West Midlands Police shows the moment an officer locates Day after he called 999. When quizzed on his story in the early hours of the morning, he insisted the dog 'just attacked me'. The footage captured Day, from Redditch, as he sat on steps while blood from his gash dripped on to the ground near the junction of Highview Street and Brewery Street. Not convinced by his lies, officers question Day on where gaffer tape wound around his injured hand had come from. He tells them he 'bought it' before saying 'it was in my car' - which he said was parked up somewhere he could not remember. Police continue to press Day, asking him if he has been attacked while a male officer tells him that his 'story does not quite check out'. Day says: "I don’t know if it was a wild dog or a fox." The officer then says "so where did this actually happen?", with the killer abruptly answering back with "I said I don't know". Day was taken to Russells Hall Hospital by paramedics who soon arrived at the scene. There, he continued to be 'cagey' before eventually accepting his wound was caused by a knife. The Dexter fanatic - who was then 19 and living with his parents - is seen in the footage lying on a hospital bed as he is arrested on suspicion of murder on Saturday, December 21. READ MORE: Unique chance to get BirminghamLive Premium for under 50p a week The trial heard how Ms Saceanu, originally from Romania, was murdered after she was contacted by Day through a website using a burner phone. The 24-year-old was 'lured' to the property, where she suffered 78 knife wounds - including some inflicted after she had died. The prosecution told the jury that Day's 'actions were those of a copycat intimidating the things he had seen' in Dexter. The programme follows character Dexter Morgan, a forensic scientist working in a police department who is a serial killer and 'knows how to' cover up what he has done. Prosecutor Rachel Brand KC said that there was 'no dispute from the defence in this case that his fascination with that programme, Dexter, played a part in his actions leading up to the night that Ms Saceanu was killed'. It was anticipated that Day was to claim self-defence, insisting he set up the room to film a 'tribute' to Dexter to post on TikTok. Ms Saceanu 'took fright when she saw how he had staged the room' and attacked him, Day was to say. READ MORE: Secret to getting the best of BirminghamLive's stories Day was arrested wearing a Dexter-style khaki top with buttons halfway down. Detectives later found a disturbing 'shopping list' on his mobile, which he had drafted a month earlier. On it were knives, scissors, a mask, an apron, disposable gloves, duct tape, a staple gun, cleaning chemicals, a pipette, a duffle bag, latex gloves, number plates and 'Hefty bags' - what Americans use to describe heavy-duty black bin bags.
